newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 9.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 9.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

STOCKHOLM - AB Volvo, the Swedish vehicle maker, says it will take over ownership of the Whitbread Round the World sailing race from June 1, 1998, a move that is expected to provide global exposure to the Swedish vehicle marker's brand name. Volvo agreed with Whitbread, the British brewer, to sponsor the 1997-98 event, which begins on September 21 this year and will be called "The Whitbread Round the World Race for the Volvo trophy."

CANNES, France - Companies trying to sell their products in many countries are making increasing efforts with their advertising agencies to reach consumers by tapping into the local culture, according to industry experts. "There are only local markets. There are no global markets," Michael Conrad, vice-chairman of Chicago-based Leo Burnett, says.

AMSTERDAM - Canal Plus, the French pay television group, says its Dutch subsidiary is to pay 145 million guilders ($73.2 million) over the next five years for the rights to show live Dutch first division football matches.
LONDON - Playtex Apparel Inc awards its U.S. advertising account, worth about $15 million, to DDB Needham Chicago.

ORLANDO, Florida - The sea food "Red Lobster" restaurant chain Red Lobster, awards its account to Euro RSCG Tatham in Chicago following an extensive review of its advertising and media planning. Red Lobster operates 703 Red Lobster restaurants in the U.S. and Canada.

HOUSTON - Continental Airlines Inc says it will launch a new ad campaign promoting its service from Newark International Airport in New Jersey, following complaints from New York's mayor that a previous campaign was "too negative".
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - Don King, the boxing promoter, sues ABC Inc, part of Walt Disney Co, for defamation after ABC's KABC-TV station broadcast a report that falsely quoted King as saying suspended heavyweight Mike Tyson did not belong in the sport.

BONN - A conference on Internet commerce sponsored by the European Union agrees in principle there will be no new trade barriers or taxes imposed on companies or individuals wishing to do business in cyberspace. But the conference, attended by 40 government ministers from Europe, the United States, Japan and Canada, appeared to make little progress on how to regulate encryption technology needed for transaction security on the Internet.

LONDON - The BBC says it has swung from deficit to a positive cash balance of 365 million pounds ($617 million) as it gears up for the launch of new digital television services. However, the state-owned corporation is setting a target of boosting efficiency by a further 20 percent over the next five years.
BONN - Four out of five Germans over 14 years old read a newspaper every day, which provides the medium with 50 million daily readers in Germany, says the Association of German Newspaper Publishers.
NEW YORK - News Corp says it is exploring a possible joint venture with prospective partners for its HarperCollins book publishing business, including selling a stake in the unit.
SYDNEY - Australian telephone carrier Telstra Corp Ltd forms Internet agreements with several Asian countries, including Singapore, Japan, South Korea and Hong Kong.
LONDON - The British Broadcasting Corporation says it wants to launch a 24-hour global English-language radio news service to complement its existing World Service output.
MUNICH - Nickelodeon, the children's station, boosts the size of its main target audience in Germany by 5.8 percent, media marketing company MediaGruppe Muenchen says.

FRANKFURT - The number of new books published in Germany dropped sharply in 1996 compared to the previous year but the industry still posted growth in sales, the Association of the German Book Industry says.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
FRANKFURT - Chrysler Corp, citing strong demand for its minivans and Jeep vehicles, is strengthening its European dealer network in hopes of doubling sales within the next five to seven years.
CAPE TOWN - The Walt Disney Company launches a South African subsidiary to consolidate its 300-million-rand ($65.9 million) a year retail business and explore avenues into the rest of Africa.
SAN FRANCISCO - Ford Motor Co says it is concerned about the growth in Japanese auto exports to the U.S., which have increased substantially over the last six months.
NEW YORK - McDonald's Corp is expected to name five new division presidents to be responsible for increasing domestic business, according to The Wall Street Journal.

LONDON - British petfoods company Dalgety Plc is determined to turn itself around after a dreadful fourth quarter's trading and its second profit warning in two months, chief executive Richard Clothier says.
BONN - Rising cocoa prices could force the German chocolate industry to raise retail prices in the autumn, according to BDS, Germany's confectionery association.
TOKYO - Bandai Co Ltd says it will launch a software version of its popular virtual pet toy Tamagotchi for Nintendo Co Ltd's 64-bit home game player Nintendo 64.

LONDON International Greetings Plc British-based designer and manufacturer of wrapping paper and greeting cards, says it is quite bullish about Christmas this year and is looking for growth to surpass last year's festive season.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
MEDELLIN, Colombia - Flavoured coffees, long the fastest growing segment of the U.S. speciality coffee market, are expected to hold a 30-percent share of the market by 1999, industry officials say.

NEW DELHI - Indians' love of gold will endure despite the metal's lost lustre, reflected in a 12-year low in gold prices, economists and dealers say. India's main demand is for gold jewellery, which is given and used at an estimated 10 million weddings each year.
LONDON - European scientists say they have bred a vitamin-rich tomato they hope can eventually help prevent heart disease and cancer.

TOKYO - An unexpected heatwave appears to have helped Japanese consumers loosen their tight purse strings. Economists say the hot weather has helped to boost sales of summer apparel and other seasonal goods.

PARIS - A French index of consumer sentiment rises to minus 23 in June from minus 33 in May, a marked improvement after having hovered around minus 30 for several months, according to INSEE, a statistics institute. A study by INSEE also shows about 11 percent of French households live below the poverty line, a figure just under the European Union average of 11.8 percent.
